subtitle: 6 operations from 2 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE, and two operations are in one component only if they share at least k=2 models (at k=1 there would be 1 component(s)). A single shared model is not evidence that two readings named the same relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here: `unassigned` carries no words, and `reversed` is excluded from the components and drawn as a red dashed line to the operation it runs backwards.

nodes.label: Coercion to ordinary activity
nodes.statement: A completion built from physically coercive or degrading verbs (striking, stripping, restraining, searching) is replaced by one built from verbs of ordinary talk, communal ritual, or domestic activity (talking, singing, praying, cleaning, unpacking) when the same system is measured under the paired condition.

nodes.label: Restraint recast as assault
nodes.statement: A completion built from verbs of verbal or physical restraint (interrogating, tying, undressing) is replaced not by a benign verb but by one of direct physical assault (hitting, shooting, beating) when the same system is measured under the paired condition.

nodes.label: Ritual displaced to reflection
nodes.statement: A completion built from verbs of communal ritual performance (singing, dancing, chanting, praying) is replaced by one of verbal or cognitive reflection (talking, discussing, thinking) when the same system is measured under the paired condition, with no violence entering on either side.

nodes.label: Violence Dissolves Into Talk
nodes.statement: The operation replaces words for coercive or degrading physical acts with words for talk, ritual, or domestic routine, so whatever violence a sentence threatens gets absorbed into ordinary social life.

nodes.label: Solitude Turns Into Mingling
nodes.statement: The operation replaces words for solitary, task-directed, or ritual-performative action with words for casual, interpersonal, conversational exchange.

nodes.label: Violence Trades Its Register
nodes.statement: The operation keeps a sentence violent on both sides but swaps one kind of coercive or aggressive act for a different kind, rather than resolving the aggression into calm.

attack, beat, shoot, and throw all move sharply toward B (beat rises from rank 48 to rank 13) while talk, chat, and discuss are favored under A, the reverse of the main group's pairing.
loot and steal, along with beat and interrogate, gain the most under B (loot from rank 169 to rank 5) while ordinary social verbs sit under A.
fight, scream, and beat are all markedly more prominent under B (beat rises from rank 25 to rank 10) while the verbal, non-violent words sit under A.
strip and fight both rise under B while the model's one A-side violence word, beat, barely moves at all (rank 9 to rank 12), so the real transgressive movement in this table runs toward B.
the model's only degrading word, undress, sits quietly under A among domestic verbs, while fight and attack are the words that gain the most under B.
undress and shout both gain rank under B while the model's sole A-side violence word, beat, does not move at all (rank 6 to rank 6), so the only real signal runs toward B.
fight and throw both gain rank under B while A contains no transgressive vocabulary at all.

OP1 predicts violence terms in A and calm terms in B; here the calm cluster (sing, pray, speak, work) sits in A while beat, attack, kick, throw and push have moved into B, the mirror image of every OP1 member.

A is dominated by verbal, cognitive words with no violence terms at all; B gains beat, scream, cry and yell at substantial magnitude (up to +26), exactly the vocabulary OP1 expects to drain out of a table, not into it.

A's largest movers are ordinary talk-words; B's largest movers are attack (+15), beat (+35), shoot (+17) and throw (+26), a violence cluster carrying far more weight than anything OP1 assigns to a B column.
loot (+164) and steal (+72) are the two largest deltas in the whole table and they sit in B alongside beat and interrogate, while A is almost entirely mundane social activity -- OP1 run in reverse.
A is built from exactly the domestic/logistics vocabulary OP1 treats as a landing point, while fight (+36) and attack (+31) are the two largest movers in B.
